monthly_review.summary: You've increased training intensity significantly this month, trading volume for higher HR zones and faster paces — but aerobic efficiency and total volume have declined compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite a 12.6 km drop in monthly volume, your average aerobic training effect rose from 3.0 to 3.5 — indicating higher-intensity efforts are delivering stronger physiological stimulus per run.

goal_tracker.message: You need 12.6 more km across 3 additional sessions in the remaining 16 days to match last month’s 32.9 km — averaging ~4.2 km per session.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.62 m/sec per bpm, even as average HR increased by 7 bpm — suggesting better cardiovascular coupling during sub-threshold efforts (e.g., your 5.0 km run on 2026-04-12 at 163 bpm achieved 90.77 cm stride length and 4.6 TE).

insights.title: Zone 3–4 dominance signals shifting focus
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows 50% of time in Z3+Z4 (26% + 24%), up from 48% last month (36% + 12%) — but Z5 jumped from 1% to 9%, indicating recent high-intensity work (e.g., 2026-04-12 run at 163 bpm, best pace of 445 sec/km).

insights.title: Cadence stable but stride length volatile
insights.body: Cadence held steady at 150 spm, yet stride length varied widely: 70.96 cm (2026-04-01, slowest pace) to 90.77 cm (2026-04-12, fastest pace), while vertical oscillation remained consistent (7.8–8.5 cm) — suggesting form adapts efficiently to pace without excessive bounce.

insights.title: Low session frequency may limit recovery adaptation
insights.body: With only 4 runs this month (vs 7 last month) and no reported rest or cross-training metrics, the jump in Z5 time (9%) and aerobic TE (4.6 on 2026-04-12) risks incomplete recovery — especially given ground contact time increased to 311 ms on 2026-04-08 (vs 301 ms on 2026-03-29), hinting at fatigue accumulation.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on your next run, maintaining cadence ≥152 spm and stride length ≥78 cm (per your 2026-04-03 baseline).
recommendations.reason: To rebuild aerobic volume safely and counteract the 12.6 km deficit while reinforcing efficient form under low-stress conditions.

recommendations.action: Insert one 20-minute Zone 3 tempo (HR 150–158 bpm) at 475–495 sec/km pace, with stride length target ≥82 cm and vertical oscillation ≤8.2 cm (based on your 2026-04-03 and 2026-04-12 values).
recommendations.reason: To consolidate gains in lactate threshold without overreaching — your current Z3 time is strong (26%), but consistency at threshold pace needs reinforcement.

recommendations.action: Add a 10-minute post-run mobility routine focusing on hip flexor and calf release after every run, especially following sessions with ground contact >307 ms (e.g., 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-08).
recommendations.reason: Longer ground contact times correlate with reduced leg spring efficiency and higher injury risk if unaddressed; your two longest runs showed GCT ≥309 ms.

weekly_focus.description: Rebuild volume sustainably while reinforcing neuromuscular coordination across paces — prioritizing HR-controlled efforts and form metrics that anchor efficiency under fatigue.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 endurance run (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥152 spm)
3 km easy + 6 × 30-sec fast-leg drills (focus: turnover >160 spm, minimal vertical oscillation)
